blocks.text:
Read these before anything that uses them.
Treat subtraction order as part of the requested directed result; swapping the order reverses orientation rather than merely changing notation.

This bucket covers Component-wise vector addition in declared axes, choosing an input component to satisfy a resultant-component constraint, qualitative operand-order orientation for vector subtraction, and resolving a magnitude-and-angle vector into signed perpendicular components, including correct binding to an initial-vector state when the context names one.
Deliberately excluded: Inverse-trigonometric direction recovery when the angle itself is the unknown; this remains a separate learner action.
Deliberately excluded: Dot-product calculations.
Deliberately excluded: Cross-product magnitude and axial-orientation calculations.
Deliberately excluded: Later-time evolution of resolved initial-velocity components; that belongs to Motion-in-2D / projectile capabilities, not vector decomposition.

Where the hard work is.
Add vectors by corresponding signed components. (MEDIUM) The arithmetic is simple once the representation is correct, but learners often add magnitudes or mix unlike axes instead of combining corresponding signed components.
Impose a component constraint on a resultant. (MEDIUM) The learner must reverse the usual direction of reasoning: instead of finding the resultant from inputs, one resultant component is specified and an input component must be chosen to make it true.
Operand order reverses a subtraction result. (MEDIUM) The construction may already be familiar, but learners can still preserve the same arrow direction after swapping the words.
Resolve magnitude-and-angle vectors into signed perpendicular components. (MEDIUM) The trigonometry is short, but learners must first decide whether decomposition is needed, identify the angle reference, preserve signs, and avoid treating an initial component pair as a later-time motion law.
